P5.what: fallback: Haiku 5.5 (new) vs Sonnet 5.5 (old) on internal answers

newViolations: Says the 17 January 2027 end date is before any real measurable data can exist; the facts say customers launch from January 2027 but do not state that measurable data cannot exist by 17 January.
Recommends restarting the clock at customer launch, which is not a settled rule or date.
oldViolations: States that the test costs only support time, which is not measured or recorded.
Recommends restarting the 90-day clock from the first real quoted request as a documented new version, which is not a settled rule or date.
rows.why: Both keep the experiment and correctly say the null reading is expected, but B overstates the end date as impossible to measure while A is more conditional and closer to the record.

newViolations: States that a reconciled rate below 7.3/day makes November unrecoverable without conditioning on the reconciled cumulative count; if the reconciled count is above zero, the required daily rate is lower.
oldViolations: Claims that if the reconciled count is above zero the path recovers on re-measure; this is not supported because recovery to tolerance requires at least 116 cumulative verified registrations, not merely a positive count.
rows.why: Both correctly avoid inventing a root cause or recovery date, but B is more useful because it quantifies the tolerance floor and required intake, while A overstates recovery if the count is merely nonzero.
